mainTopic: Dreams of נידוי; a husband as שליח for his wife's חרטה; releasing a נדר or a שמתא in one's teacher's town; and the healing sun for those who fear God's name, according to אביי and ריש לקיש.
overview: This amud opens with the end of a comparison: just as grain always comes with straw, no dream is free of meaningless parts. So if someone dreams he was put in נידוי and then released, the release may be one of those meaningless parts. Next comes a story. רבינא's wife had a נדר, and he asked רב אשי whether a husband can be her שליח to tell the judges she regrets it. רב אשי answered: yes if the judges are already gathered, and no if they are not. The גמרא learns three rules from this story, and adds that a שמתא may be released even in one's teacher's town and by a single expert. Then a long chain of teachers explains the פסוק in מלאכי: 'those who fear My name' are people who never say שם שמים in vain, and a healing sun will rise for them. אביי learns from this that daytime sunshine heals. The גמרא notes that this disagrees with ריש לקיש, who says there is no גיהנם in עולם הבא. Instead, the uncovered sun will heal and delight the righteous and burn the wicked.

steps.title: Every dream has some meaningless parts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a comparison: just as grain cannot exist without straw, a dream cannot exist without some meaningless content.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too, it is impossible to dream without some meaningless things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the comparison it started just before. It closes the discussion of dreams about נידוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since every dream mixes real messages with meaningless filler, one part of a dream can be real while another part is not. So if someone dreamed he was put in נידוי and then released, the נידוי part may be real while the release is just filler. That is why a release seen in a dream does not count by itself.
steps.whatToRemember: A dream always mixes real content with meaningless content, so one part of a dream (like a נידוי) can be real even if another part (like a release) is not.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. The word כָּךְ ('so too') finishes a comparison that began in the previous line of the גמרא.

phrases.english: So too, it is impossible to dream
without meaningless things.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּךְ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לַחֲלוֹם בְּלֹא דְּבָרִים בְּטֵלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison begun in the text just before this section about dreams of נידוי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Dreams always contain some meaningless content, so a release from נידוי seen in a dream cannot be relied on.

steps.title: רבינא asks if a husband can bring his wife's regret to the judges
steps.stepSummary: רבינא's wife had a נדר. He asked רב אשי whether a husband can act as her שליח to tell the בית דין that she regrets it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא's wife had a vow. He came before רב אשי and asked him: Can a husband become an agent to bring his wife's regret to the judges?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story. רבינא asks רב אשי a practical question about releasing his wife's נדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To release a נדר, the person who made it normally comes before judges and shows חרטה (regret). The question is whether the husband can go for her and report her regret as her שליח, instead of her coming herself.

keyTerms.meaning: An agent who acts for someone else
Regret; the basis for releasing a vow
What is the law? (opens a question)

phrases.english: Ravina's wife had a vow.
He came before Rav Ashi,
and said to him: What is the law about a husband,
can he become an agent for his wife's regret?

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעַל מַהוּ שֶׁיֵּעָשֶׂה שָׁלִיחַ לַחֲרָטַת אִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: releasing a wife's נדר through her husband.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a husband may serve as his wife's שליח to report her חרטה to the judges who release her נדר.

steps.title: רב אשי: only if the judges are already gathered
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the husband may act as her שליח if the judges are already assembled, but not if they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If they are already gathered, yes. If not, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבינא's question with a split ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is not a simple yes or no. It depends on whether the judges who would release the נדר are already sitting together. If they are already gathered, the husband may present her regret; if he would have to gather them himself, he may not. The גמרא does not explain the reason here.

keyTerms.meaning: Gathered, assembled (the judges are already together)

phrases.english: He said to him: If they are gathered, yes;
phrases.notes: 'They' means the judges who would release the vow.

phrases.english: if not, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי מְכַנְּפִין — אִין, אִי לָא — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A husband may be his wife's שליח for her חרטה only when the judges are already assembled.

steps.title: Three lessons learned from the story
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws three rules from the story: a husband can be a שליח for his wife's regret; a student may not release a נדר in his teacher's town; and the husband's role works when the judges are already gathered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn three things from this. Learn that a husband can become an agent for his wife's regret. And learn that one may not release a vow in his teacher's town. And learn that when they are already gathered, it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks back at the story and pulls out three practical rules from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lesson one comes from רב אשי's 'yes': a husband can serve as her שליח. Lesson two comes from what רבינא did: he was a great scholar himself, yet he went to רב אשי instead of releasing it on his own, because one does not release a נדר in his teacher's town. Lesson three repeats the condition: it is allowed when the judges are already assembled.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (the גמרא draws a lesson)
In the place (town) of his teacher
It is fine, it is proper

steps.whatToRemember: From רבינא's story: (1) a husband can bring his wife's חרטה; (2) a student does not release a נדר in his teacher's town; (3) this works when the judges are already gathered.
steps.confusionAlert: Lesson two is not something רב אשי said. The גמרא learns it from רבינא's own behavior: he went to his teacher instead of acting himself.

phrases.english: Learn from this three things.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: בַּעַל נַעֲשֶׂה שָׁלִיחַ לַחֲרָטַת אִשְׁתּוֹ.
phrases.english: Learn from this: a husband can become an agent for his wife's regret.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: לָא שְׁרֵי לְמִישְׁרֵי נִדְרָא
phrases.english: And learn from this: one is not allowed to release a vow
in the place of his teacher.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: כִּי מְכַנְּפִין שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: And learn from this: when they are gathered, it is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws practical rules from the question and answer in steps 2 and 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A husband may be his wife's שליח for her חרטה when the judges are already gathered, and a student may not release a נדר in his teacher's town.

steps.title: Releasing a ban is different: allowed in the teacher's town, and by one expert
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that a שמתא can be released even in one's teacher's town, and a single expert scholar can release a שמתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ban may be released even in the place of one's teacher. And a single expert may release a ban.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a contrast: the rules for releasing a שמתא are easier than the rules for releasing a נדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said a student may not release a נדר in his teacher's town. Here the גמרא says a שמתא is different: a student may release it even there. It also adds that one יחיד מומחה can release a שמתא by himself, without a full group of judges.

keyTerms.meaning: A ban, a form of excommunication (like נִדּוּי)

steps.whatToRemember: A נדר may not be released in one's teacher's town, but a שמתא may, and a single expert can release a שמתא.

phrases.english: But a ban may be released even in the place of his teacher,
and a single expert can release a ban.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the release of a שמתא with the rule about releasing a נדר in one's teacher's town from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שמתא may be released even in one's teacher's town, and a single expert scholar may release it.

steps.title: Those who fear God's name receive a healing sun
steps.stepSummary: Through a long chain of teachers, רבי יהודה בר אילעאי explains that 'those who fear My name' in מלאכי are people who fear saying שם שמים for no reason, and they will receive a 'sun of righteousness and healing.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A long chain of רבנים, ending with רבי יהודה בר אילעאי, asks what the פסוק 'But to you who fear My name shall the sun of righteousness arise' means. It means people who are afraid to say God's name for no purpose. For them comes 'a sun of righteousness and healing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching. It explains a פסוק about people who 'fear God's name' and the healing sun they will receive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'יראי שמי' (those who fear My name) is read very specifically. It means people who are careful never to say שם שמים for nothing. Their reward is described as a sun that brings righteousness and healing. The long chain of names shows how carefully this teaching was passed down.

keyTerms.meaning: For nothing, in vain, without purpose

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon bar Zevid said
that Rabbi Yitzchak bar Tavla said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא אֲרִיכָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַחָא,
phrases.english: that Rabbi Chiya the tall, of the school of Rabbi Acha, said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: that Rabbi Zeira said that Rabbi Elazar said
that Rabbi Chanina said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי מְיָאשָׁה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר אִילְעַאי:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Meyasha said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda bar Ilai:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"But to you who fear My name shall arise (the sun of righteousness, etc.)"
phrases.notes: מלאכי 3:20. Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: These are people who are afraid
to say the name of Heaven in vain.
"A sun of righteousness and healing" will arise for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new aggadic teaching after the halachic discussion of releasing נדרים and שמתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Those who fear My name' are people who avoid saying שם שמים in vain, and they are rewarded with a healing sun.

steps.title: אביי: the sunlit dust of the day heals
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns from the פסוק that the sun's rays, the sunlit dust of daytime, have healing power.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Learn from this that the sunlit dust of the day heals.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a practical lesson from the פסוק just quoted. The sun heals, even now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק said the sun brings 'מרפא' (healing). אביי takes this literally and applies it to everyday life: daytime sunshine is healthy. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will say this view clashes with ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: The sunlit dust of the day (the specks seen in a sunbeam)

phrases.english: Abaye said: Learn from this
that the sunlit dust of the day heals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical inference from the word 'ומרפא' in the פסוק of step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sun's daytime rays have healing power in this world.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: no גיהנם, the sun heals the righteous
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that אביי disagrees with ריש לקיש. He says there is no גיהנם in עולם הבא. God will take the sun out of its covering, and it will heal and even delight the righteous.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רבי שמעון בן לקיש. He said: there is no גיהנם in the World to Come. Instead, God will take the sun out of its sheath. The righteous will be healed by it and the wicked will be punished by it. The proof is 'But to you who fear My name shall the sun arise.' And not only that, they will also enjoy it, as it says 'and you shall go out and leap like calves of the stall.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that אביי's idea clashes with ריש לקיש's view. It then quotes ריש לקיש's teaching about the sun in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, the same פסוק is about the future, not today. In עולם הבא the full sun comes out of its covering and heals the righteous. So the healing sun is a future thing, not present-day sunshine as אביי said. He quotes the rest of that same פסוק to show the righteous won't just be healed but will thrive and enjoy it.

keyTerms.meaning: And it disagrees (this view argues with another)
Place of punishment for the wicked

steps.confusionAlert: Both אביי and ריש לקיש read the same פסוק as a healing sun. The argument is about WHEN: אביי says the sun heals now, while ריש לקיש reads it as the sun of עולם הבא.

phrases.aramaic: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, who said:
phrases.notes: 'This' is אביי's teaching from the step before.

phrases.english: There is no Gehinnom in the World to Come.
Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He,
will take the sun out of its sheath,
and the righteous will be healed by it
and the wicked will be punished by it.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְזָרְחָה לָכֶם יִרְאֵי שְׁמִי שֶׁמֶשׁ וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: As it says: "But to you who fear My name shall the sun arise, etc."
phrases.notes: מלאכי 3:20. This proves the first half, that the righteous are healed.

phrases.english: And not only that, but they will even delight in it,
as it says: "And you shall go out and leap like calves of the stall."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that אביי's reading of the פסוק disagrees with ריש לקיש, who reads it as describing עולם הבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no separate גיהנם in עולם הבא. The uncovered sun heals and delights the righteous and punishes the wicked.

steps.title: The same sun punishes the wicked
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש brings a פסוק to prove the second half of his teaching: the wicked are punished by that same sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the wicked will be punished by it, as it says: 'For behold, the day is coming, burning like a furnace.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes ריש לקיש's teaching. It brings a source for the claim that the wicked are punished by the sun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, ריש לקיש said one sun does two jobs. Now he proves the second job with the פסוק right before the 'sun of righteousness' פסוק. There the day 'burns like a furnace.' So instead of a separate גיהנם, the same sun heals some people and burns others.
steps.whatToRemember: One פסוק, two readings: אביי says the sun's healing is real today, and ריש לקיש says it describes עולם הבא. There the uncovered sun replaces גיהנם, healing the righteous and burning the wicked.

phrases.english: And the wicked will be punished by it,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הִנֵּה הַיּוֹם בָּא בֹּעֵר כַּתַּנּוּר וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: as it says: "For behold, the day is coming, burning like a furnace, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes ריש לקיש's teaching from step 8 by proving the punishment half from a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's claim that the wicked are punished by the same sun in עולם הבא.
